figures.caption: Fig. 3 | The effect of DTA in fully-connected networks. Panels a–b show the results after applying the neighbor-DTA. Panel a presents the order parameter R for different coupling strength λ with different attention weight α (red: 0; yellow: 0.5; blue: 1). The vertical line indicates the critical coupling strength λc ≈ 2.28 obtained analytically. Panel b shows the analytical approximation (solid curve) and numerical results (dots) of the critical coupling strength λc for different α. Panels c–d show the results after applying the self-DTA. Panel c presents the order parameter R for different λ and α. The vertical line indicates the critical coupling strength λc ≈ 2.28 obtained analytically when α = 0. Panel d shows the critical coupling strength λc for different α with distinct attention decay rate (red: β = 1; blue: β = 0.01).

Fig. 4 | The effect of DTA in the WS networks. Panels a–d and e–h show the results after applying the neighbor- and self-DTA. In all cases, the natural frequency distribution is set as g(ω) = δ(0). a, Order parameter R for different coupling strength λ under different attention weight (red: α = 0; yellow: α = 0.5; blue: α = 1) when attention decay rate β = 1. b, Order parameter R versus λ with the same settings as those in panel a except that β = 0.01. c, Critical coupling strength λc for different α under distinct β (red: 1; yellow: 0.1; blue: 0.01). d, Order parameter R for different α with fixed λ = 1.5. e, Order parameter R for different coupling strength λ when β = 1. f, Order parameter R versus λ when β = 0.01. g, Critical coupling strength λc for different α. Non-monotonicity appears for small β (yellow and blue). h, Order parameter R for different α with fixed λ = 1.5. The non-monotonicity is consistent with that in panel g.

Fig. 1 | Emergence Transformer and emergent coherence. a Illustration of phase, query, key and value matrices and the attention kernel together with the attention information used for updating the phase dynamics. b, The dynamics of a phase oscillator θ(i) in Emergence Transformer is affected by the current states (blue circles) and attention information (green squares) of its neighbors (depending on the network topology), its own natural frequency ω(i) and noise. c, A natural scenario of the accumulation of the attention information of an oscillator. It is accumulated from all of its past states (blue circles) with an exponential decay rate β. Light and dark green represent the attention information with large and small decay rate, respectively. The schematic diagram shows a discrete-time case just for the sake of better understanding. d, The Emergence Transformer with the neighbor-DTA. e, The Emergence Transformer with the self-DTA. f, The coherence characterizes the level of synchronization by using the classical order parameter R. g, Synchronizability refers to the propensity to synchronization. Larger critical coupling strength λc corresponds to lower synchronizability.

Fig. 6 | The effect of DTA for the emergence of continual learning in the HNN. a, The HNN is designed for recovering the masked pattern (red: masked; yellow: original). The letter is not recovered without attention. By applying appropriate DTA, the recovery is successful. We consider 7 letters ‘KURAMOT’ in this work. The rest of panels show, in ϵ-α parameter space, the leading (right-most) eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix of the synchronization state corresponding to each letter: b, ‘K’; c, ‘U’; d, ‘R’; e, ‘A’; f, ‘M’; g, ‘O’; h, ‘T’. The heatmap show the stable region (red) and the unstable region (blue) for each pattern. The black solid curve represent the boundary between stable and unstable regions.

Fig. 2 | Overview pictures of how DTA affects the coherence. In all schematic diagrams, we use ten individuals for clarity. The results are actually obtained for populations with more individuals (see Methods for parameters used). Blue dots represent the snapshot of phase oscillators after a sufficiently long time period and yellow pentagram indicates the order parameter (coherence). a, Fully-connected (spatial) network with the neighbor-DTA. As attention weight α increases, the coherence keeps static. b, Fully-connected network with the self-DTA. Increasing α suppresses the coherence. c, The WS network with the neighbor-DTA when attention decay rate is large (β = 1). Increasing α promotes the coherence. d, The same settings as those in panel c are applied except that the self-DTA is used which suppress the coherence. e, The WS network with the neighbor-DTA when attention decay rate is small (β = 0.01). Increasing α promotes the coherence. f, The same settings as those in panel e are applied except that the self-DTA are used. Increasing α first promotes and then suppress the coherence which is a non-monotonic behavior.
